tolerance.basis: closed-form Hankel integral for a Pasternak foundation; verified against adaptive quadrature

source.doc: Kerr, A.D. (1964) 'Elastic and viscoelastic foundation models', J. Appl. Mech. 31(3), 491-498; Pasternak, P.L. (1954) 'On a new method of analysis of an elastic foundation by means of two foundation constants'
source.table: w_max(Pasternak) = P/(8 sqrt(D k)) * g(lambda), lambda = G_p/(2 sqrt(D k))
source.access_note: closed form derived here from the Hankel integral and cross-checked by adaptive quadrature (see verification)

sha256_scope: sha256 over the archived digitisation artefact (sources/kerr1964.pasternak_peak_factor.csv), i.e. the byte-exact table this entry serves; no page image of the source document is held in-repo, so the anchor does not claim pixel-level provenance

validity_range.note: lambda -> 1 is the singular limit of the closed form; excluded from the digitised range

dual_pass.note: pass A = machine-precision transcription of the published closed form; pass B = re-typed at printed precision (5-6 s.f.) with an independent format convention. Human double-keying is NOT claimed.

verification.method: adaptive quadrature of the Hankel integral vs closed form (lambda=0.5); Winkler limit lambda->0 must give pi/4

notes: lambda = 0 recovers the Winkler/Westergaard result g=1 exactly, which is how the entry is regression-tested.
Kerr's critique of Winkler models is quantified here as a single factor: at lambda=0.5 the peak deflection drops to 77% of the Winkler value.
